material_declarations.name: SimpleGraph
material_declarations.meaning: An undirected graph with symmetric, irreflexive adjacency.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The vertex type Fin N fixes the host order. The set filter counts neighbors inside the chosen set.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: SimpleGraph.induce
material_declarations.meaning: Restriction of both adjacency arguments to the subtype of selected vertices.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Comap along the subtype embedding retains every internal edge.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: SimpleGraph.degree
material_declarations.meaning: Number of neighbors in the induced graph.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The finite neighbor set consists exactly of vertices adjacent to the chosen vertex.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Real.log
material_declarations.meaning: Natural logarithm on positive reals.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Inverse of the real exponential there. The value at zero is zero and a finite initial segment has no effect on little-o.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Real.exp
material_declarations.meaning: Real exponential, used for absolute sizes, probability rates and relative cut scales.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Real part of the complex exponential on the real axis.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Nat.ceil
material_declarations.meaning: Least natural number above the real input.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The ceiling adjunction yields the explicit inequality used to round the scale.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Asymptotics.IsLittleO
material_declarations.meaning: For every positive ε the magnitude of log g(k) is eventually bounded by ε times k.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The constant in IsBigOWith is universally quantified before the eventual bound.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Filter.atTop
material_declarations.meaning: Filter of tails in the ordered index.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Intersection of the principal filters of upper intervals. At natural or real indices, eventual membership has a single lower threshold.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Filter.Eventually
material_declarations.meaning: A property holds for all sufficiently large indices.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The set of satisfying indices belongs to the indicated filter, here atTop.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Filter.Tendsto
material_declarations.meaning: The dyadic rate divided by log(2^j+1) eventually exceeds each fixed real bound.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The image filter lies below atTop. Both ordered tails appear in the proved threshold characterization.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Disjoint
material_declarations.meaning: Two finite sets share no member.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The only common lower bound of their subsets is empty.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Nat.Prime
material_declarations.meaning: A prime natural has size at least two and no proper divisor above one.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The definition uses irreducibility. Its positive-divisor characterization is a theorem.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Nat.ModEq
material_declarations.meaning: The two counts have equal remainders modulo q. The conclusion negates this relation.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Remainder equality on natural numbers.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: IsSquare
material_declarations.meaning: The additive declaration Even z is generated from IsSquare by to_additive. It means z = x + x for an integer x.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Parity is evaluated on the signed difference, including negative differences.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: ZMod
material_declarations.meaning: Integers modulo a positive q, including composite q.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Its carrier for q = n+1 is Fin (n+1), with modular addition and multiplication.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: dotProduct
material_declarations.meaning: Sum of the coordinatewise products over the finite index set, computed modulo q.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The vector dimension bounds the number of summands.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: ZMod.stdAddChar
material_declarations.meaning: Additive character sending the residue of z to exp(2πiz/q).
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The circle-valued character is composed with the map to the complex numbers.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Matrix.mulVecLin
material_declarations.meaning: Linear map acting by matrix-vector multiplication.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Its additive image controls complexity for composite moduli through cardinality.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: AddMonoidHom.range
material_declarations.meaning: Image subgroup of the underlying additive map.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The to_additive declaration has carrier equal to the set of values on all input vectors.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: AddSubgroup
material_declarations.meaning: Additively closed subgroup containing zero and closed under negation. Membership of x−z in H specifies a translated coset.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The carrier and closure under addition and zero are inherited from the additive submonoid.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Nat.card
material_declarations.meaning: Natural cardinality of the subgroup or image, finite in every use here.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Cardinal.toNat agrees with Fintype.card on finite enumerated types.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Fintype.piFinset
material_declarations.meaning: All indexed choices from the coordinate pools, with order and repetitions.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: A function belongs exactly when every coordinate belongs to its assigned set.
material_declarations.proof_status: Relevant finite and ordered specializations are checked through each of the two independent entrypoints.

excerpts.name: Real.log
excerpts.text:
/-- The real logarithm function, equal to the inverse of the exponential for `x > 0`,
to `log |x|` for `x < 0`, and to `0` for `0`. We use this unconventional extension to
`(-∞, 0]` as it gives the formula `log (x * y) = log x + log y` for all nonzero `x` and `y`, and
the derivative of `log` is `1/x` away from `0`. -/
@[pp_nodot, wikidata Q11197]
noncomputable def log (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if hx : x = 0 then 0 else expOrderIso.symm ⟨|x|, abs_pos.2 hx⟩

excerpts.name: exp_log
excerpts.text:
theorem exp_log (hx : 0 < x) : exp (log x) = x := by
  rw [exp_log_eq_abs hx.ne']
  exact abs_of_pos hx

  ∀ᶠ x in l, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖g x‖

  simp only [IsLittleO_def, IsBigOWith_def]

theorem prime_def_lt {p : ℕ} : Prime p ↔ 2 ≤ p ∧ ∀ m < p, m ∣ p → m = 1 :=
  prime_def.trans <|
    and_congr_right fun p2 =>
      forall_congr' fun _ =>
        ⟨fun h l d => (h d).resolve_right (ne_of_lt l), fun h d =>
          (le_of_dvd (le_of_succ_le p2) d).lt_or_eq_dec.imp_left fun l => h l d⟩

excerpts.name: IsSquare
excerpts.text:
/-- An element `a` of a type `α` with multiplication satisfies `IsSquare a` if `a = r * r`,
for some root `r : α`. -/
@[to_additive /-- An element `a` of a type `α` with addition satisfies `Even a` if `a = r + r`,
for some `r : α`. -/]
def IsSquare (a : α) : Prop := ∃ r, a = r * r

theorem mem_piFinset {t : ∀ a, Finset (δ a)} {f : ∀ a, δ a} : f ∈ piFinset t ↔ ∀ a, f a ∈ t a := by

  · simp only [piFinset, mem_map, and_imp, forall_prop_of_true, mem_univ, exists_imp,
